items.t: Bradner is a rural acreage community in west Abbotsford centred on Bradner Road.
Bradner Elementary at 5291 Bradner Road and Bradner Hall at 5305 Bradner Road sit side by side and anchor the village core.
The community runs toward Mt. Lehman and the Township of Langley line on its west side, with Matsqui Prairie to the north and east.
Housing here is detached homes on rural acreage lots, not strata subdivisions.
Bradner Hall states the present hall was erected by local volunteers in 1900 and the Bradner Community Club was established in 1924.
The hall states capacity of up to 350 and use by 4-H clubs, a fitness group and local sports teams.
ALR rules cap house size and second homes on farm parcels here, as across Abbotsford.
A principal residence in the ALR is capped at 500 m² total floor area; exceeding it needs a Non-Adhering Residential Use application to the Commission.
An additional residence beyond what the ALR Use Regulation permits also needs Commission permission, and the Commission must not grant it unless it is necessary for a farm use.
Abbotsford farm parcels here fall under the Agricultural zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014, including the A2 zone referenced in current council reports.

items.t: The Bradner Flower Show has been held at Bradner Hall since 1932, per the hall's own history.
The hall and the elementary school share the same short stretch of Bradner Road, 5291 and 5305 Bradner Road.
Wind-erosion and ditch rules for the prairies also govern field edges here: City procedure addresses vegetation removal beside ditches and ditch cleaning in Matsqui and Sumas Prairies.
The nearest City capital work read is the Clayburn Creek Improvement Project in Matsqui Prairie, status Current, outside Bradner's core.
Bradner owners pay Abbotsford general taxes plus any district levies that apply to their parcel.
The 2026 Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026 sets separate dyking and drainage districts for the prairies; whether a Bradner lot is inside one must be checked on its tax notice.
Where City water and sewer exist, the March 1, 2026 residential rates are $1.46/m³ water and $1.35/m³ sewer.
Abbotsford is a designated Speculation and Vacancy Tax taxable area.
Bradner Road is the spine road; there is no rapid transit in this rural area.
BC Transit Central Fraser Valley route 21 Aldergrove/Abbotsford is the inter-city route on the west side of Abbotsford listed in the current route set.
Highway 1's 264 Street interchange is the Langley-side freeway access for the Bradner/Mt.
Verify ALR status, well water potability and septic condition on any acreage before offering.
Check the parcel against the provincial dike inventory and City drainage maps if it drains toward Matsqui Prairie.
Confirm whether an existing second building was built with ALC and City permits; oversize or extra residences need Non-Adhering Residential Use approval.

blocks.text: Surrounded by farmland and partly in the Agricultural Land Reserve, Bradner is a small, historic rural centre on Abbotsford’s west side.

faq.q: Is there a community hall and what happens there?
faq.a: Yes, Bradner Hall at 5305 Bradner Road is the community centre. Its own site states the Bradner Community Club was established in 1924, the present hall was erected by local volunteers in 1900, the hall has been home to the Bradner Flower Show since 1932, and the facility holds up to 350 people for catered functions and local groups including 4-H clubs.

faq.q: Which school do Bradner children attend first?
faq.a: Bradner Elementary on Bradner Road is the local elementary school. The Abbotsford School District lists Bradner Elementary School at 5291 Bradner Rd, Abbotsford, beside the hall, with the school site at bradner.abbyschools.ca. Catchments in rural Abbotsford go by street address, so confirm the exact address with SD34 before removing subjects on any purchase.

faq.q: Can I add a second dwelling for family on an acreage?
faq.a: Only within the ALR residence rules, which are restrictive. Provincial policy allows generally one residence per parcel, permits an additional residence only where the ALR Use Regulation conditions are met, and otherwise requires a Non-Adhering Residential Use application; the Commission must not approve an additional residence unless it is necessary for a farm use.

faq.q: Is Bradner on city water and sewer?
faq.a: What is confirmed is the municipal utility pricing structure: from March 1, 2026 Abbotsford residential water is $1.46/m³ and sewer is $1.35/m³ where City services exist. Lots outside service areas rely on private well and septic arrangements, which need their own inspections.

faq.q: Can I build a second house on a Bradner farm property?
faq.a: Only within the ALC limits: one principal residence per parcel (maximum 500 m²), a secondary suite only inside that residence, and an additional small residence for farm use or another permitted use — maximum 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha.

faq.q: Is Bradner in the Agricultural Land Reserve?
faq.a: Partly — Bradner is a rural agricultural community on Abbotsford's west side, with lands zoned A1 and A2 Agricultural under the City of Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw and part of the area in the ALR; whether a specific parcel is in the ALR must be confirmed for that parcel.

faq.q: Can a suite go in a barn or a detached building on ALR land?
faq.a: No — under the ALC housing rules a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence; a detached second dwelling is the "additional residence," which is size-capped and tied to farm use or another permitted use.
